note: Three selective 5-HT6 antagonists were pro-cognitive in rat memory models and reached their occupancy or exposure targets in humans, yet idalopirdine (three Phase 3s), SAM-760 and masupirdine all failed on ADAS-Cog as add-ons to cholinesterase inhibitors.
label: Alzheimer's (5-HT6)

engagement.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
engagement.model: Rat in-vivo striatal 5-HT6 occupancy ([3H]Lu AE60157) with subchronic-PCP NOR
engagement.note: Idalopirdine's rat occupancy ED50 (2.7 mg/kg) and plasma EC50 (20 ng/mL) were set; no human occupancy for idalopirdine was ever published.
engagement.short: Rat occupancy ED50 set, never checked in humans
engagement.quote: Orally administered Lu AE58054 potently inhibited striatal in-vivo binding of the 5-HT(6) antagonist radioligand [(3)H]Lu AE60157 ([(3)H]8-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)-3-phenylsulfonylquinoline), with an ED(50) of 2.7 mg/kg.
engagement.judgement: Opens the idalopirdine track at the first published in-vivo occupancy/efficacy paper (Lundbeck). The PD readout the model used was striatal receptor occupancy, so readout_tier is direct.

engagement.note: Pfizer measured SAM-760 5-HT6 occupancy by PET in monkeys before the human PET study (NCT01258751, posted 2010-12-13).
engagement.short: Monkey PET occupancy run before human PET
engagement.quote: Based on pre-clinical evidence, brain penetration and target engagement of PF-05212377 was confirmed in NHP using positron emission tomography (PET) measured 5-HT6 receptor occupancy (%RO).
engagement.judgement: Opens the NHP occupancy track at the proxy year the model was first used (human PET study NCT01258751 registered 2010-12-13; AAIC abstract 2011).

The Atri 2018 Discussion, which may describe the healthy-volunteer PET basis for the 10-60 mg doses, could not be retrieved (scrape truncated); if it reports occupancy, this track's engagement becomes same.
engagement.strengthens: Adds the registry record that a human occupancy comparison was attempted (AD-patient PET, 2017) and terminated unreported, so the untested status is a documented gap, not an absence of trying.

engagement.magnitude_basis: unbound plasma EC50 for 5-HT6 occupancy: NHP 0.31 nM vs human 0.37 nM
engagement.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the human PET study NCT01258751 has no posted results.
engagement.note: Monkey unbound-plasma EC50 for occupancy (0.31 nM) matched the human PET value (0.37 nM); humans reached ~80% occupancy at >=15 mg.
engagement.short: Monkey occupancy EC50 matched human PET
engagement.quote: In conclusion, cumulative evidence from NHP and human PET RO assessments confirmed that NHP is more appropriate than the rat for the prediction of human brain penetration of PF-05212377, a P-gp/non-BCRP substrate.
engagement.reason: Monkey occupancy EC50 matched human PET
engagement.judgement: Not a retrodiction: both the NHP and human PET were run prospectively in 2010-11 (NCT01258751) before the Phase 2; only the peer-reviewed comparison came late (2023), so year is 2023 and retrodiction false. Healthy volunteers count for engagement.

engagement.magnitude_basis: unbound brain/plasma ratio, rat 0.05 vs NHP 0.64 (the value human PET occupancy was consistent with)
engagement.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
engagement.model: Rat unbound brain/plasma ratio (P-gp substrate) as predictor of human CNS penetration
engagement.note: Rat predicted poor CNS exposure (unbound brain/plasma 0.05) yet humans reached ~80% 5-HT6 occupancy, matching the monkey (0.64).
engagement.quote: Species differences were observed in the in vivo brain penetration of PF-05212377 with a ratio of the unbound concentration in brain/unbound concentration in plasma (Cbu /Cpu ) of 0.05 in rat and 0.64 in non-human primates (NHP).
engagement.judgement: Scored contra because the paper itself states the rat was the wrong species for predicting human brain penetration of this P-gp substrate; the failed model keeps its own track and the NHP that did better is a separate track.

engagement.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Herrik 2016 (epub 2016-03-31). Amat-Foraster 2017 (frontal gamma, awake EEG; 10.1016/j.neuropharm.2016.09.017), Mork 2017 (mPFC microdialysis; 10.1016/j.ejphar.2017.02.010) and Ferris 2017 (awake fMRI; 10.3389/fphar.2017.00279) extend the same system.
engagement.model: Rat hippocampal ACh microdialysis and nPO-evoked theta/gamma oscillations with donepezil
engagement.note: Idalopirdine potentiated donepezil's hippocampal ACh rise and theta/gamma power in rats; neither ACh nor EEG oscillations were ever measured in idalopirdine-dosed humans.
engagement.short: Rat ACh/EEG potentiation, no human PD
engagement.quote: This study demonstrates that idalopirdine potentiates the effects of donepezil on two pharmacodynamic biomarkers associated with cognition, i.e. neuronal oscillations and extracellular ACh levels in the hippocampus.
engagement.reason: No human ACh or EEG readout published
engagement.judgement: Separate track from the rat occupancy/PCP-NOR system (rat-subchronic-pcp-nor): a different model (donepezil co-administration, PD biomarkers) making a different prediction (idalopirdine adds to an AChEI). The four Lundbeck papers (electrophysiology, microdialysis, fMRI) are one system with one prediction, so one model_id. No idalopirdine EEG, microdialysis or fMRI study in humans was registered or published, so the readout was never checked.

dose.quote: Steady-state modelling of an acute pharmacokinetic/5-HT(6)R occupancy time-course experiment indicated a plasma EC(50) value of 20 ng/ml.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the idalopirdine track.

dose.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5887246); registry results NCT01712074 posted 2017-03-20, earlier than the 2018 paper, so year is 2017.
dose.note: 30 mg saturated 5-HT6 receptors in humans, the occupancy the monkey model targeted; the Phase 2 was stopped for futility on ADAS-cog13.
dose.short: Occupancy saturated at 30 mg, trial futile
dose.quote: Despite a human positron emission tomography (PET) study indicating saturation of the 5-HT6 receptor at the 30-mg QD dose, there was no significant difference compared with placebo for the primary endpoint (ADAS-cog13).
dose.reason: Target occupancy reached; drug failed; abandoned
dose.judgement: Reached, failed, abandoned: contra derived from efficacy. The efficacy failure itself is not scored on a model track because Pfizer published no SAM-760 disease-model efficacy data; Fullerton 2018 went to Phase 2 on class clinical data plus human occupancy. Fullerton calls the outcome unexplained ('precise reasons ... are unknown'), hence source_calls_it unresolved. The paper puts human occupancy beside the outcome; the model side (NHP) is paired by me, so comparison_stated false with model_src Sawant-Basak 2023.

dose.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
dose.confidence_note: The Atri 2018 Discussion (dose-selection rationale, any PET occupancy data) could not be retrieved: Europe PMC and NCBI PMC full-text XML returned nothing and the Firecrawl scrape truncated before the Discussion. Abstract and Methods only.
dose.model: Rat in-vivo striatal 5-HT6 occupancy ([3H]Lu AE60157) with subchronic-PCP NOR
dose.note: Phase 3 used 10-60 mg/d, below the 90 mg/d that worked in Phase 2; whether the rat occupancy/exposure target was met at these doses is unpublished.
dose.short: Phase 3 dosed below Phase 2, target unverified
dose.quote: Idalopirdine (10, 30, or 60 mg/d) or placebo added to cholinesterase inhibitor treatment (donepezil in studies 1 and 2; donepezil, rivastigmine, or galantamine in study 3).
dose.judgement: Left untested rather than contra: the rule's 'reached, failed' row needs evidence the model's target was reached, and no human occupancy or plasma-vs-20 ng/mL comparison is public (the AD-patient PET NCT03307993 was terminated unreported). If Atri's Discussion reports healthy-volunteer occupancy at 30-60 mg, this becomes contra derived from efficacy; if it shows the doses sat below target, contra with magnitude. Year is the STARSHINE registry results date (2017-09-19).
dose.strengthens: Adds the Phase 3 regimen (10-60 mg/d, below the 90 mg/d that worked in Phase 2) and the trial outcome; shows the dose question was live and left unverified at the program's end.

efficacy.note: Idalopirdine reversed a PCP-induced recognition deficit in rats at >65% occupancy; a schizophrenia-cognition model carried into AD.
efficacy.quote: The results indicate that Lu AE58054 is a selective antagonist of 5-HT(6)Rs with good oral bioavailability and robust efficacy in a rat model of cognitive impairment in schizophrenia.
efficacy.judgement: The only published efficacy model for idalopirdine is a schizophrenia-cognition model; Lundbeck's AD rationale rested on 5-HT6 blockade potentiating donepezil (Herrik 2016, Mork 2017 rat microdialysis/EEG), published after LADDER.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; NCT01019421 has no posted results.

patient_trials.quote: Idalopirdine improved cognitive function in donepezil-treated patients with moderate Alzheimer's disease.

efficacy.model: Rat subchronic-PCP novel object recognition deficit
efficacy.note: LADDER: 90 mg/d idalopirdine on donepezil improved ADAS-cog by 2.16 points vs placebo at 24 weeks in moderate AD (primary met).
efficacy.quote: At week 24, the change from baseline in ADAS-cog total score was +1·38 (SD 0·53) in the placebo group and -0·77 (0·55) in the idalopirdine group (treatment difference of -2·16 points, 95% CI -3·62 to -0·69; p=0·0040).
efficacy.judgement: Scored on what was known in 2014 (rule 7): the model predicted pro-cognitive effect and the Phase 2 primary endpoint agreed in direction. Pairing made by me (Arnt 2010 vs Wilkinson 2014); Lundbeck's later rat papers cite LADDER but a citation is a pairing, not a stated comparison.

In study 2, the mean change in ADAS-Cog total score between baseline and 24 weeks was 1.01 for the 30-mg dose of idalopirdine group, 0.53 for the 10-mg dose group, and 0.56 for the placebo group

efficacy.model: Rat subchronic-PCP novel object recognition deficit
efficacy.note: Three Phase 3 trials (2,525 patients, 10-60 mg/d on a cholinesterase inhibitor) showed no ADAS-Cog benefit at 24 weeks; program ended.
efficacy.short: Three Phase 3 trials null on ADAS-Cog
efficacy.quote: In patients with mild to moderate AD, the use of idalopirdine compared with placebo did not improve cognition over 24 weeks of treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Contra beats the earlier same on the same track. Magnitude 'null' (no effect in patients where the model predicted one). Caveat recorded, not scored: Phase 3 doses (10-60 mg/d) were below the 90 mg/d that worked in LADDER, so the Phase 3 null is confounded by dose as much as by the model; the dose cell carries that. The SAM-760 Phase 2 (Fullerton 2018) and intepirdine Phase 3 failures are not scored here: SAM-760 has no published disease-model efficacy data and intepirdine is not a member of this tile.

efficacy.model: Rat donepezil-potentiation PD models (hippocampal ACh, network oscillations)
efficacy.note: Run after LADDER (2014): rat potentiation of donepezil's ACh and oscillation effects is offered as the mechanism of LADDER's 2.16-point ADAS-cog gain.
efficacy.short: Reproduces LADDER add-on benefit, post hoc
efficacy.quote: Such potentiation could contribute to the procognitive effects of idalopirdine observed in donepezil-treated AD patients.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: LADDER (Wilkinson 2014) was known and is cited in the abstract as the premise ('A recent phase 2 trial showed ...'), so retro, not same (decision 10). Mork 2017 Eur J Pharmacol states the same comparison more explicitly ('may provide a mechanistic model for the pro-cognitive effects ... in the phase 2 studies (Wilkinson et al. 2014)'). Direction only: the rat readouts are PD biomarkers, not cognition.

efficacy.model: Rat donepezil-potentiation PD models (hippocampal ACh, network oscillations)
efficacy.note: The model's prospective prediction, an add-on benefit on donepezil, failed in three Phase 3 trials (2,525 patients, 10-60 mg/d on a cholinesterase inhibitor).
efficacy.quote: In patients with mild to moderate AD, the use of idalopirdine compared with placebo did not improve cognition over 24 weeks of treatment.
efficacy.reason: Rat add-on synergy; three Phase 3 nulls
efficacy.judgement: First prospective test after the retrodiction (decision 10): the model was published in 2016, the Phase 3 results in 2017. Contra beats the retro on the same track. Phase 3 doses (10-60 mg/d) were below LADDER's 90 mg/d, but the add-on was tested at the occupancy target (>80% at 30-60 mg/d per Atri's Discussion), so the null is not a dose miss. Atri 2018 does not put the rat model beside the result, so the pairing is mine (model_src Herrik 2016).

efficacy.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record only: 38 subjects, 5-way crossover, single doses 5/20/60 mg vs donepezil 10 mg, Groton Maze Learning Task primary; completed 2011-08, no results posted. Not reported in Fullerton 2018 (PMC5887246 full text searched for 'scopolamine') nor in any PubMed-indexed SAM-760 paper.
efficacy.model: Healthy-volunteer scopolamine challenge (CogState battery, donepezil 10 mg positive control)
efficacy.note: Pfizer's proof-of-mechanism: SAM-760 5-60 mg against scopolamine deficits in 38 healthy adults (2010-11); never reported, so the Phase 2 futility cannot be compared.
efficacy.short: Human scopolamine challenge run, never reported
efficacy.quote: It is hypothesized that PF-05212377 (SAM-760) will reverse scopolamine induced cognitive impairments in healthy adults subjects.
efficacy.judgement: A human pharmacological challenge is a model system (brief: 'the system was not an animal'). It existed and was used for a member drug before Phase 2 (NCT01712074, 2012), but no admissible result exists to compare with the Phase 2 futility stop (Fullerton 2018), so untested rather than an empty list. Engagement and dose cells are not opened: the challenge is itself a human readout and no exposure target from it is public.

safety.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD dementia, add-on to a cholinesterase inhibitor
safety.confidence_note: No member of this class reached an NDA, so no nonclinical review exists; the toxicology species and findings for idalopirdine, masupirdine and SAM-760 are not public. Abstract-level reading.
safety.model: IND-enabling toxicology (species and findings unpublished; no NDA, so no FDA review)
safety.note: Idalopirdine caused asymptomatic transient transaminase rises in LADDER; whether animal toxicology predicted a hepatic signal is unpublished.
safety.quote: 25 patients (seven taking placebo and 18 taking idalopirdine) discontinued treatment because of adverse events, the difference between groups being mainly due to asymptomatic transient increases in transaminase concentrations in some idalopirdine-treated patients.
safety.judgement: Untested rather than an empty list: toxicology studies existed (INDs were opened for all three members) but nothing public compares them with patients. Phase 3 idalopirdine TEAEs were similar to placebo with Hy's-law monitoring (Atri 2018); SAM-760 (Fullerton 2018) and masupirdine (Nirogi 2022) were reported safe and well tolerated, so no patient harm exists to score a silence against.
